_comment: Default parameters for the map's scenario/route editor (see transitLOS/costs.md for the cost research and reasoning behind every number below). Edit this file, or a per-study copy of it, to change the editor's behavior without touching code. All costs are in millions of USD (2024-2025). All speeds are km/h.
_modes_comment: BRT visually uses the bus icon but scores (mode_score, in stop_score) exactly as tram -- see transitlos.scoring.mode.MODE_SCORES and this project's mode.py docstring for why tram/BRT are grouped together as the higher-quality-than-bus tier.

default_grade_separation._comment: Applied automatically to a segment's grade_separation when it is first created (new route or new segment) and nothing has been explicitly chosen yet -- must be one of grade_separations[mode] above. rail has no 'separated' option (its at-grade tier is called 'normal'), so it maps there instead.

grade_separation_colors._comment: Used to color the route being actively edited when the grade-separation buttons are showing (draw/extend mode) -- otherwise the route displays in its own route_color.

speeds._comment: Fixed by explicit user instruction, not derived from cost research. Dwell time is added per stop and is NOT user-configurable in the editor UI.

costs._comment: cost_per_km_musd = construction cost per route-km at that grade separation. station_musd = cost per station at that grade separation (a station's grade separation = the more expensive of its two adjacent segments', per the editor's rule -- see costs.md).

vehicle_cost_musd._comment: Item 7: per-vehicle purchase cost (millions USD), used with the classic fleet-size formula vehicles_needed = ceil(round_trip_time_minutes / headway_minutes) to estimate a route's vehicle-fleet cost. Bus cheapest, rail/tram most expensive, consistent with real procurement costs. Grade separation does NOT change the vehicle price (only whether/how much dedicated infrastructure gets built, in `costs` above) -- notably bus-in-mixed-traffic still buys vehicles even though it has ~$0 infrastructure cost, since a bus route obviously needs buses.

headway_aggregation._comment: Very simple frequency-addition when combining an edited/new route's headway with a stop's existing (already-aggregated) headway, per explicit instruction: no directional computation, no special stop-level modeling. Same-mode routes at a shared stop combine; different-mode routes at a shared stop are scored independently (not aggregated together).

access_recompute._comment: Client-side, frontend-only recompute of level_of_service for new/edited stops after the user clicks Compute.
access_recompute.max_walk_distance_m_comment: Outer straight-line catchment radius around each new/edited stop, in metres. Mirrors the real pipeline's own outer walk-distance cutoff (the last entry of the study's `walk_distance_steps`, 2000 m for Boston, forwarded to `distance_matrix.build_intelligent_distance_matrix(max_walk_distance_m=...)`). A cutoff is REQUIRED here because `walk_decay` is an offset-power curve that never actually reaches zero -- without one, every stop would touch the entire metro's population grid.
access_recompute.headway_cv_comment: Fixed headway coefficient of variation fed to `reliability_score` for editor-created routes: a drawn route has no timetable, so its real service variability is unknowable. 0.3 is the same representative value the map's Discretization tab holds reliability at (`__DISC_STOP_SCORE_DEFAULT_CV`), so the editor and that tab's curves agree.
access_recompute.method_comment: Straight-line (as-the-crow-flies) distance from each res-11 H3 cell centroid to the nearest new/edited stop, NOT a street-network walk distance -- an intentional simplification for a fast, purely-client-side what-if tool, per explicit instruction. Uses the same transitlos.scoring.walk_access decay curve shape as the real pipeline, mirrored in JS.

impact_score._comment: impact = sum(access_gain_i * population_i) over affected h3 cells. impact_per_million_dollar = impact / (total_cost_musd). Emoji thresholds are on impact_per_million_dollar.

scenarios._comment: 'current' is the reserved, non-editable scenario name representing today's real transit network -- see the editor's scenario-selection UI.
